title: scheduled_class
description: A scheduled class: one date, one time, one room at one venue, with its instructors and capacity. It is the unit people are assigned to. class_type says what kind it is: private (one person, a couple or a family), group (a leader bringing a network of people) or workshop (the public workshop people pick from a list). Private and group classes are created by processing when a request is accepted (source_request_id says which); workshops are created from the dashboard. It carries references (venue, instructors, promotions) and summary numbers (registered, waitlist, attended, reviews). Venues, instructors, reviews, attendance and promotions are their own collections. Fields marked readOnly are set by the server only. Cross-field rules the schema cannot express are endpoint rules: capacity_minimum <= capacity_target <= capacity_max; venue_room_label names a room in the venue's rooms list, and capacity_max is not above that room's max_occupancy. Only a class in status enrolling accepts registration requests. Endpoint rules: a class request may only pick a class of type workshop that is public and enrolling; source_request_id is for private and group classes only.
x_retention: Keep classes until the owner deletes them. (A written policy only; nothing enforces it yet.)

slug.description: A short unique identifier: lowercase letters, digits and underscores. Never changes once set. Required.

class_type.description: What kind of scheduled class this is: private (one person, a couple or a family), group (a leader bringing a network of people) or workshop (the public workshop people pick from a list). Required. A registration request of type class can only pick a workshop.

program_slug.description: Which program this class belongs to, as a slug such as launch. Required; the dashboard fills in launch unless told otherwise. It lets one system serve many programs and territories: search all classes for one program. Becomes a program_id (a UUID) when programs get their own record.

description.description: A few sentences about the class for the public list, free text up to 2000 characters. Optional.

status.description: Where the class is in its life, in order: identified (an idea, no date), scheduled (date and venue set), enrolling (taking registration requests), completed, or cancelled. Only enrolling accepts registration requests; any other status gives the class_closed error. Once scheduled, enrolling or completed the class must have starts_at, time_zone, duration_minutes, venue_id and is_venue_confirmed; once enrolling or completed it must also have price_cents and price_basis. Required.

cancelled_reason.description: Why a cancelled class was cancelled, free text. Optional.

is_public.description: Whether the class appears in the public list. Whether a private class can still take requests by direct link is an open decision. Required.

starts_at.description: When the class starts (UTC, ISO 8601). Empty while the class is only an idea. Required once scheduled.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone name such as America/Denver, so the start time can be shown in local time. Required once scheduled.

duration_minutes.description: How long the class runs, in minutes (15 to 600). Required once scheduled.

venue_id.description: UUID of the venue record where the class is held. The venue holds the address, contacts, rooms and standing details, so every class there reuses them. Required once scheduled.

venue_room_label.description: The label of a room in that venue's rooms list. The room must exist, and capacity_max should not be above that room's max_occupancy (an endpoint rule, not a schema rule). Optional.

is_venue_confirmed.description: Whether the venue has been confirmed with the venue (true) or only chosen (false). Required once scheduled.

venue_notes.description: Anything specific to this class at this venue, for example "use the side entrance". Not for standing venue details, which belong on the venue record. Optional.

accessibility_notes.description: Anything about accessibility specific to this class. The physical accessibility facts live on the venue record. Optional.

organizer_name.description: The class organizer's name (for now, Todd). Personal data. Never shown in the public class list.

organizer_email.description: The class organizer's email. Personal data. Never shown in the public class list.

organizer_phone.description: The class organizer's phone. Personal data. Never shown in the public class list.

instructor_ids.description: UUIDs of the instructors teaching the class (up to 10, no repeats). Their names and contact details live in a person schema that is not written yet.

capacity_minimum.description: How many people must be registered for the class to run. Must not be above capacity_target (an endpoint rule). Required.

capacity_target.description: The number planned for ("we'll take it to 10"). Must be between capacity_minimum and capacity_max (an endpoint rule). Required.

capacity_max.description: The absolute ceiling ("we'll go as high as 15"). The range from capacity_target to capacity_max is overflow; there is no separate overflow field. A registration request is refused (over_capacity) only when its attendee_count is over this number. Required.

is_waitlist_enabled.description: Whether the class keeps a waiting list. A waitlisted person is still a registration request; processing decides whether a request is accepted, accepted into overflow, or waitlisted.

waitlist_max.description: How long the waiting list may grow (0 to 500). Optional.

price_cents.description: What the class costs, in US cents. Zero means free. Read with price_basis, so the price shown on a request can be compared with it. Required once enrolling.

price_basis.description: What price_cents covers: per_session (the whole session) or per_person (each attendee). Required once enrolling.

promotion_ids.description: UUIDs of promotion records (channel, link, cost) for this class, so a promotion's success can be measured. A request carries the optional promotion_code from the link.

id.description: UUID v4, set by the server; also the Firestore document id. Never sent by a browser.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written under (currently 2). Set by the server.

created_at.description: When the record was created (UTC, ISO 8601). Set by the server.

created_by.description: Who created the record, as an actor string such as user:<uuid>. Set by the server.

updated_at.description: When the record last changed (UTC). Set by the server.

updated_by.description: Who last changed the record, as an actor string. Set by the server.

source.description: Where the record came from: dashboard or import. Set by the server. Classes are created from the dashboard, never by a public page.

previous_id.description: Id of the earlier record this one follows or replaces; a rescheduled class can point at the one it replaces. Set by the server.

source_request_id.description: Id of the registration request this class was created from. Private and group classes only: processing creates the class when it accepts the request. Set by the server. Workshops never carry it.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete time: the record is kept, never hard-deleted. Set by the server.

deleted_by.description: Actor who soft-deleted the record. Set by the server.

registered_count.description: How many people are registered for the class. Starts at zero and is kept current as requests are processed. Set by the server.

waitlist_count.description: How many people are on the waiting list. Starts at zero and is kept current as requests are processed. Set by the server.

attended_count.description: How many people attended, kept current from the attendance collection (not written yet). Starts at zero. Set by the server.

review_count.description: How many reviews the class has, kept current from the reviews collection. Starts at zero. Set by the server.

average_rating.description: Average of the class's review ratings, 1 to 5. Absent until the first review exists. Set by the server.
